h2: Radiographic testing in Dallas–Fort Worth: Texas licensing, radiographer certification and site work
html:
Radiographic testing in Dallas–Fort Worth: Texas licensing, radiographer certification and site work

Industrial radiography in Dallas–Fort Worth is regulated by the Texas Department of State Health Services, because Texas is an NRC Agreement State. A crew working in the Metroplex needs a state radioactive materials license or X-ray registration that covers field work, and every radiographer needs Texas certification or accepted reciprocity. Atlantis confirms the radiography arrangements for each job before a crew leaves Houston.

What Texas asks of the radiographer. The licensing and registration rules sit in 25 TAC §289.255. For individual certification, DSHS requires a 40-hour radiation safety course, trainee status, and documented on-the-job training under a supervising trainer: at least 200 hours for radioactive material work and 120 hours for X-ray work, or a year of industrial radiography experience in another state. Candidates then pass a written examination at a Pearson VUE center, and holders of certain other recognized certifications can apply through reciprocity. Hours spent on film interpretation, darkroom work, travel and classroom time do not count toward the on-the-job total.

That card covers radiation safety. It is separate from the RT Level I or Level II certification an employer issues under its SNT-TC-1A written practice, which covers technique and film interpretation. Ask any RT supplier for both, together with the license or registration covering the source or X-ray tube they will bring to your site. Texas radiographer certification has to be renewed, so check the expiry date on each card rather than only confirming that one exists.

Where radiography is used around DFW.

  • Weld repairs on boilers regulated by the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation, where the repair documentation goes to the insurer's commissioned inspector
  • Girth welds on gas gathering, transmission and distribution replacement work to API 1104; Atmos Energy and Energy Transfer are both headquartered in Dallas
  • Pressure vessel and piping spool fabrication to ASME Section VIII and B31.3, with the radiographs kept in the data book
  • Tie-in welds on compressor and meter station piping serving Barnett Shale gathering systems west of Dallas
  • Castings and assemblies in the Fort Worth aerospace supply chain, where NAS 410 personnel certification applies

Site practicalities. Radiography in a built-up metro area needs exclusion zones, posted boundaries and often night or weekend shifts so the plant or street can be cleared. Where those limits make film radiography slow, digital radiography shortens exposure and removes chemical processing, and TOFD or phased array UT can replace radiography where the construction code and client allow it. The method itself is explained on the radiographic testing page, and site scopes that mix RT with other methods start from NDT inspection services.

For technicians: the RT training course and the Practical NDT radiography simulator cover method theory and interpretation for SNT-TC-1A certification. The Texas radiation safety course and DSHS examination are separate requirements. To book site radiography, send weld counts, thicknesses, access hours and the governing code through the Dallas–Fort Worth RT request.
